features.name: Fetch Records node: palette, config panel, test run, Run for, @ picker (Phases 5–6)
features.description: Workflow Builder support for the backend `fetch-record-node`; (`services/cadp_workflow_backend_nodejs/docs/changes/fetch-record-node.md`).; **Node registration:** `fetch-record-node` in the `WorkflowNodeType` union, a; `NODE_DEFINITIONS` entry (category action, "Fetch Records"; `defaultConfig` copied key for; key from the backend catalog), and the Database icon in the 3 icon maps.; **Branch handles:** `found`, `empty`, plus `error` when Continue On Error is on; (`branchUtils.getNodeBranchDefinitions`). These are the labels the engine routes on.; **Config panel** (`FetchRecordConfigPanel`, routed by type in `NodeConfigPanel`, the same; pattern as Approval Gate). Sections:; 1. Source: module, feature, optional Data Table.; 2. Filter: nested ALL/ANY groups with `@`/`{{}}` token values; skip-blank and; include-deleted toggles.; 3. Result: single / list / count / exists / aggregate; fields to return; group by,; aggregates and having; sort; limit.; 4. Output: output variable (validated `^\w+$`), output rows field, when nothing is found,; continue on error, timeout.; **Downstream tokens:**; `useUpstreamSources` derives a Fetch node's outputs from its returned fields and; aggregate aliases: `{{<nodeId>.record.X}}` / `{{<nodeId>.rows[0].X}}`, count, found.; It no longer lists the fetched feature as an upstream *trigger* feature (its values do; not come from the trigger record).; `useFieldTagging` offers upstream Fetch outputs even when the caller passes none, and; `{{row.X}}` entries ("Fetch row" group, listed first) when the step's Records Field equals; a Fetch node's Output Rows Field.; **Run for** (`RunForSelector`, shown above Create / Update / Upsert / Delete):; Options are "This trigger record" or "Each row from: <Fetch node>", and it writes; `recordsField`.; Switching back to the trigger record asks for confirmation when `{{row.…}}` tokens are; used.

whatToTest: Roles assigned by their record ID now load correctly — `getRolesByNamesAndTenantId` matched a user's role refs against `roleId` and; a misspelt `__id` field that no role has, so a role referenced by its Mongo `_id`; never matched. It now matches `roleId` or `_id` (for refs that are 24-hex ObjectIds),; the same way the workspace-access checks in `user.workspace.service.js` already do.; Empty/missing refs skip the query and return `[]`, the same result as before.
knownIssues: Because some menu structures have changed, certain features may return a 403 status code. To resolve this, edit the role, select the platform feature, and save the role again.
Use the conventional feature-wise approach wherever workflow scheduling is required.
Formula Builder UI – Field Insertion Through Typing
This works in current fields. For external feature fields, it won't work, as there could be fields with same names from multiple features.
Formula Builder – AI-Based Formula Writing/Editing Not Implemented
Organization Details → Basic Info: Website URL accepts invalid URL formats without validation.
Expected: Validate the URL format and show an error message for invalid values, such as www.example or example@123.www.example
Builder Tool Not Available on Mobile Web
The builder tool is not supported on mobile web. This is implemented as expected — builder functionality is restricted to desktop browsers by design. It should be available on Tab though.
Mobile – Formula Field Not Working in Tables & Charts
Formula fields are not evaluated correctly when used inside Tables and Charts on mobile. This is under review.
apiChanges: All external-database endpoints moved to cadp_dbsync_backend_nodejs

Follow-up to the Database Sync move below: the rest of the external-database; code moved to `cadp_dbsync_backend_nodejs` as well, so master no longer contains any.; Endpoints: `/external-db/explore`, `/query`, `/aggregate`, `/export`, `/bulkdataFetch`,; `/distinct-values`, `/select`, `/select/validate` (plus `/test-query`, `/test-connection`; moved earlier).; Code: `external-db-explorer.controller.js`, `external-db-select.controller.js`, their; routes, `external-db-{aggregate,distinct,explorer,export,page,select}.service.js`, and; the whole `src/service/external-db/` folder including the SQL core (`core/`).; Tests: external-db-page, external-db-select, external-db-statement-timeout and the nine; sql-core-* suites moved with the code.; Master keeps the shared helpers that other code uses: `constants/dacFilterOperators.js`; (extraction DTO), `utils/filterGroupUtils.js`, `communicators/client.ws.service.js`.; `data-archival/rules/readOnly.rules.js` still lists `/external-db/*` as read-only routes;; those entries no longer match anything in master and are harmless.; The external-DB change logs (external-db-explorer.md, external-db-sql-core.md,; external-db-dac.md) were copied to the dbsync repo; the copies here are marked moved.
Database Sync moved out of master into cadp_dbsync_backend_nodejs

Database Sync now runs in its own service, `cadp_dbsync_backend_nodejs`.; Master no longer runs syncs or serves the query builder's test endpoints.; **Moved out of master** (now in the dbsync repo): the scheduled run; (`GET /database-sync/run/:featureId`), scheduler registration (create/recreate/remove; the notification-service task), `bulkSyncFeatureData`, `reconcileFullSyncDeletes`,; `resolveImportFieldMetadataForFeature`, `ensureSyncMatchIndex`,; `external-db-query.controller/service/routes` (`POST /external-db/test-query`,; `POST /external-db/test-connection`), `external-db/json-path-explode.js`,; `external-db/row-group-in-memory.js`, and the notification-service connector.; The import/auto-ID helpers those methods call stay in master (regular imports use; them); dbsync carries its own copy of the 48 methods the sync needs.; **Master still** validates and saves the feature's `databaseSync` config. After a; save that touched config, and after a feature delete, it now calls; `POST {DBSYNC_SERVICE_URL}/database-sync/schedule/:featureId` (new; `communicators/dbsync.service.js`); the dbsync service owns the scheduler task and; stores `schedulerTaskId`/`schedulerTriggerId` on the feature. Still fire-and-forget.; The frontend calls `/dbsync/external-db/test-query` through the RBAC gateway's new; `/dbsync` proxy.; The dbsync service adds a per-feature run lock (one run per feature across all its; pods) and a 30-minute scheduler timeout for sync actions. Overlapping runs were; visible in UAT logs: a run longer than the scheduler's 5-minute HTTP timeout was; retried while still running.
Workspace list: page size capped at 100, version lookup scoped to the page

`GET /workspaces/workspacesList` now caps `limit` at 100 (minimum 1, default; 10) and treats an invalid or < 1 `page` as 1. The response's `pagination.limit`; reports the capped value. The active-version lookup now reads only the page's; workspaces and only `{ workspaceId, version }`, instead of the full active-version; record of every workspace in the tenant. `getAllActiveVersions(workspaceIds)` keeps; its old behaviour when called without ids; `findLatestActiveByFilter` takes an; optional projection. Also fixed: with `limit=1` and a pinned workspace, page 1; ran `.limit(0)`, which Mongo treats as "no limit", so it returned every workspace.; That query is now skipped.
configChanges: Vault secret names for AI builder / LLM gateway switched to kebab-case

`runtime-bootstrap.js` now resolves `AI_BUILDER_BASE_URL`, `AI_BUILDER_USERNAME`,; `AI_BUILDER_PASSWORD`, `AI_BUILDER_HIERARCHY`, `LLM_GATEWAY_URL` and `LLM_GATEWAY_API_KEY` from the; vault secrets `ai-builder-base-url`, `ai-builder-username`, `ai-builder-password`,; `ai-builder-hierarchy`, `llm-gateway-url` and `llm-gateway-api-key` (previously the UPPER_SNAKE names).; Env var names consumed by the code are unchanged.
The vault keys were renamed to kebab-case to match the other secrets.
Faster workspace-access lookup and perf measurement in RBAC

New roles index `{ tenantId: 1, workspaceId: 1, roleId: 1 }`. The only existing index; starts with `roleName`, but the role lookups made on every authenticated request; (`getRolesByNamesAndTenantId`) and by `GET /users/workspace`; (`getWorkspaceIdsWithDirectRoles`, `getWorkspaceIdsWithGroupRoles`) filter on; tenantId/workspaceId/roleId and never on roleName, so they could not use it.; Mongoose `autoIndex` builds it on each tenant DB the first time the Role model is; bound there after deploy (non-unique, no data changes).; `getWorkspaceIdsByTenant` (`GET /users/workspace`) now selects only the user fields; it reads instead of the whole user document. Response unchanged.; Ported master's perf measurement (`src/utils/perf-metrics.js`,; `src/middleware/perf-timing.middleware.js`): per-request timing with Mongo op; count/time, `[perf] slow mongo command` (≥ `PERF_SLOW_MONGO_MS`, default 100),; `[perf] slow outgoing http` (≥ `PERF_SLOW_HTTP_MS`, default 500), and a periodic; per-route p50/p95/p99 summary. Same `PERF_*` env vars as master. Because every; browser request passes through RBAC, `[perf] request` lines default to requests; ≥ 500 ms (`PERF_LOG_MIN_MS`). Requests forwarded by the proxy routers group by; their id-normalised path, tagged `[proxied]`. Log lines carry field names only,; never values, bodies or tokens.

master logged `[perf] slow outgoing http` for; `GET localhost:3001/rbac/users/workspace` at 2,890 ms on; `GET /master/workspaces/workspacesList` in UAT, and RBAC had no measurement to show; which step was slow.
LLM gateway URL resolved from vault

`runtime-bootstrap.js` now maps `LLM_GATEWAY_URL` from the vault secret `llm-gateway-url`.; Optional; falls back to the `.env` value / built-in default as before. The API key still comes from; each saved LLM integration.
Aligns with master backend's vault key naming.

Ported master's perf measurement (`src/utils/perf-metrics.js`,; `src/middleware/perf-timing.middleware.js`): per-request timing grouped by Express; route with Mongo op count/time, `[perf] slow mongo command`; (≥ `PERF_SLOW_MONGO_MS`, default 100), `[perf] slow outgoing http`; (≥ `PERF_SLOW_HTTP_MS`, default 500) and a periodic per-route p50/p95/p99 summary.; Same `PERF_*` env vars as master. Most traffic here is master's service-to-service; role checks, so `[perf] request` lines default to requests ≥ 500 ms; (`PERF_LOG_MIN_MS`). Log lines carry route templates, collection and field names; only, never values, bodies or tokens.
master could see that client-ws role checks were slow; (`POST /role/view/features`, 1,199 ms in UAT) but client-ws had no measurement to; show which step was slow.
AI builder credentials resolved from vault

`runtime-bootstrap.js` now maps `AI_BUILDER_BASE_URL`, `AI_BUILDER_USERNAME` and; `AI_BUILDER_PASSWORD` from the vault secrets `ai-builder-base-url`, `ai-builder-username` and; `ai-builder-password`. Optional; `.env` values still apply when the secret is absent.
Aligns with master backend so AI workflow generation reads credentials from the vault; instead of plaintext env files (addresses the follow-up above).
